Let me evaluate against the rubric.

C1 Mission concept: Clear goals, objectives, requirements, users, needs, references. Accomplished. Mark 9.

C2 Project plan: Gantt chart, task descriptions, contingencies, information sources, fits mission narrative. Accomplished. Mark 9.

C3 Preliminary progress: Hand calculations for orbit, STK tutorials, interpretation of swath trade. Good preliminary results with interpretation. Accomplished. Mark 8-9. Check calculations: a = 6978 km, T = 2π√(6978³/398600). 6978³ = 3.398e11... let's compute: 6978³ = 6978² × 6978 = 48,692,484 × 6978 ≈ 3.3977e11. Divide by 398,600 → 852,434. sqrt → 923.3 s. ×2π → 5801 s. Correct. Orbits/day 14.9. Sun-sync inclination at 600 km: ~97.8°, correct. Ground track shift: 360 × 5801/86164 = 24.24°, correct. Swath 60 km. Interpretation good. Mark 9.

C4 Presentation: Well structured, headings, figures/tables labelled, references match. Minor issues: "MECH lab 204" odd, but fine. Accomplished. Mark 8-9.

Requirements: R1 yes; R2 yes (orbit, launch in plan, course material); R3 yes (STK selected, mentions PIGI fallback with registration); R4 yes; R5 yes; R6 yes.

Technical issues: minor — 10 m GSD at 600 km requires very large aperture (diffraction limit ~ 1.22λD/... for 10 m at 600 km in visible, D ≈ 0.15 m actually feasible-ish; 10 m GSD from 600 km is like WorldView-level, plausible but ambitious for "simple" mission). Weekly cloud-free imaging of tropical Queensland is optimistic (cloud). Also "near-real-time relay" vs 24h delivery slight inconsistency. Sun-sync 600 km gives ~14.9 orbits/day; fine. Also the claim "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — surface oceans ~30% increase in acidity since industrial revolution, that's actually correct. Fine.

Overall: strong submission.
